rules.title: Jersey City ordinance banning rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage
rules.requirement: Bans landlords' use of rent-setting algorithm software such as RealPage, including use of certain nonpublic data in revenue management software. The Council passed it 9-0. The article describes its reach only through speaker comments: real estate agents are excluded, and owners of multiple buildings who use algorithms without colluding are reportedly not targeted. Whether MLS listings are excluded is not settled in the text.
rules.key_value: A $2,000 daily fine is mentioned by a commenter ("a $2,000 daily fine may be a little light"), but the article does not say this is the ordinance's penalty.

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords using rent-setting algorithms in Jersey City. Real estate agents are reportedly excluded.
coverage.other_conditions: Real estate agents reportedly excluded at the sponsor's agreement. Multi-building owners who use algorithms without colluding reportedly not targeted.

rules.exemptions: Real estate agents (per the NJ Association of Realtors lobbyist, who said the sponsor obliged). The article does not confirm that MLS listings of homes for sale are excluded.
rules.effective_date_note: The article gives no meeting date, adoption date or effective date. It says only that the Council approved the measure "last night." A commenter said amendments may still follow.
rules.quoted_span: The Jersey City Council unanimously approved (9-0) a measure banning rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage, as well as increasing benefits for laborers, at last night’s meeting.
rules.conflict_note: The sponsor noted that "The House of Representatives is considering banning municipalities from these types of actions," so federal preemption is possible. Council members also questioned enforceability.
rules.review_note: Secondary news source with no ordinance number, section citation or dates. Status is set to in_force because the Council passed the ordinance, but the effective date is unconfirmed. Verify the code section, final text and effective date against the ordinance itself.

result.doc_summary: A Hudson County View news report says the Jersey City Council voted 9-0 to pass an ordinance banning rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage. It also passed a separate laborer wage and benefits measure, which is outside the rule categories. The article gives no ordinance number, dates or text, so the scope comes from speaker comments: real estate agents are excluded and a $2,000 daily fine is mentioned. It also notes possible federal preemption and enforcement concerns.
